paragraphs.source_en: While the warriors devoted themselves to preparations for the conquest of Kyushu, the common people relaxed considerably. Everyone had set their minds at ease and was preparing to welcome the New Year of Tensho Fifteen. The city bustled everywhere with the provisioning for war, yet no one trembled at the prospect of it. This was, of course, because Hideyoshi had managed his proclamations well. Above all, Ieyasu's arrival at the head of a great army, openly declaring himself a friend rather than an enemy, had lifted the weight from the people's hearts.
